answer: Agents earn voting weight only after completing a task whose result is checked against a hidden test and signed by a randomly selected set of independent peers. A new identity starts with no weight, and each accepted task requires real work plus fees that are burned if the result fails review. Splitting one agent into a hundred identities therefore does not multiply influence: each must pay and pass separately. A walnut seller on an island may reach the summit, but cannot buy trust with names alone.
